2: To the Overseer. --`Destroy not.' --A secret treasure, by David. Is it true, O dumb one, righteously ye speak? Uprightly ye judge, O sons of men?
3: Even in heart ye work iniquities, In the land the violence of your hands ye ponder.
4: The wicked have been estranged from the womb, They have erred from the belly, speaking lies.
5: Their poison is as poison of a serpent, As a deaf asp shutting its ear,
6: Which hearkeneth not to the voice of whisperers, A charmer of charms most skilful.
7: O God, break their teeth in their mouth, The jaw-teeth of young lions break down, O Jehovah.
8: They are melted as waters, They go up and down for themselves, His arrow proceedeth as they cut themselves off.
9: As a snail that melteth he goeth on, As an untimely birth of a woman, They have not seen the sun.
10: Before your pots discern the bramble, As well the raw as the heated He whirleth away.
11: The righteous rejoiceth that he hath seen vengeance, His steps he washeth in the blood of the wicked.
12: And man saith: `Surely fruit is for the righteous: Surely there is a God judging in the earth!'
